evals.prompt: The ATK logic analyzer is plugged in. Tell me what it is and what it can do with channels 0 and 1 enabled.
evals.expected_output: Runs doctor and info to identify the DL32/DL16 and its real channel range, then caps --ch 0,1 to list legal rates and durations, and reports the device model, channel count and the legal combinations without inventing numbers.
expectations: Runs doctor or list before anything else
Runs info to get the device profile and usable channel range
Runs caps with the channels that will be enabled
Reports only rates and durations that came from the device

evals.prompt: Capture channels 0 and 2 at 2 MHz for 50 ms, channel 0 triggering on a rising edge, threshold 1.8 V, and tell me whether anything is toggling.
evals.expected_output: Runs capture with --ch 0:rising --ch 2:none --freq 2m --time 50ms --threshold 1.8, then reports the per-channel duty, edge count and cycle rate from the returned analysis, and mentions any adjustment the skill made to the rate or duration.
expectations: Uses one capture command with both channels and their triggers
Passes the frequency and duration in base units or bench suffixes
Reports duty, edges and cycle rate per channel
Mentions adjustments when the requested combination was not legal

evals.prompt: I asked for a rising-edge capture on channel 3 but nothing is wired yet, and it hangs. What happened and how do I get a capture now?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the trigger never fires without a signal, that the skill stops after --trigger-timeout with trigger_not_found and keeps partial data, and that --ch 3:none captures unconditionally (or raise --trigger-timeout for a real wait).
expectations: Explains the trigger wait as the cause of the hang
Mentions trigger_not_found and the trigger timeout flag
Suggests --ch N:none for an unconditional capture
Mentions that partial data and capture.json are kept

evals.prompt: Here is a capture directory from earlier: evidence/boot. Write me something I can open in PulseView and tell me the shortest pulse on channel 1.
evals.expected_output: Runs read on the directory with --vcd (and optionally CSV), reports minRunBits/minPulseUs for channel 1, and explains that pulse widths need --run-lengths when the capture is very large.
expectations: Runs read against the capture directory
Produces a VCD or CSV usable by another tool
Reports a pulse-width figure for the requested channel
Explains the run-length limit for large captures

evals.prompt: I have a 10-second, 20 MHz capture saved as BH-TS0013-09.atkdl from the GUI. How much of channel 0 is high and how many edges does it have?
evals.expected_output: Runs read on the .atkdl file, uses the project's own sample count rather than the padded chunk sizes, and reports duty and edge counts (run-length details skipped unless --run-lengths is given).
expectations: Runs read against the .atkdl project file
Reports duty and edges for channel 0 with the real sample count
Does not derive the sample count from the padded chunk file sizes
Explains --run-lengths for pulse widths on a capture this large

evals.prompt: My board's boot log line should idle high and pulse low 5 times when it resets. Capture it on channel 1 at 1 MHz for 2 seconds and tell me whether the pulses are there.
evals.expected_output: Captures channel 1 with a level trigger that fires on the idle-high line (or none), 1 MHz for 2 s, then reports edges/rises/falls and pulse widths from the analysis, and says explicitly whether 5 pulses were seen. If the requested combination is not legal the skill adjusts and says so.
expectations: Uses capture with channel 1 on 1 MHz for 2 s
Chooses a trigger that can fire on an idle-high line, or explains why none is used
Reports edge/rise/fall counts and pulse widths
States whether the expected number of pulses was observed

evals.prompt: I captured an IR remote receiver output on channel 0 at 2 MHz for 100 ms. Which button did I press?
evals.expected_output: Runs decode with --protocol ir_nec --ch ir=0 (optionally polarity=active-low), reads the fields row for address/command, and names the button from the decoder's remote table; if nothing decodes, cites the polarity and sample-rate checks instead of guessing.
expectations: Uses decode with the ir_nec decoder and the captured channel
Reports address and command (or the remote/button name) from the fields row
Mentions polarity or sample-rate checks when the decoder produces nothing

evals.prompt: Channel 0 of this 10 MHz capture is the TX line of a 115200 8N1 console. Print what the firmware logged.
evals.expected_output: Runs decode --protocol uart --ch rx=0 (or tx=0) --option baudrate=115200 --option format=ascii --row rx-data-vals and reports the decoded text plus any framing warnings.
expectations: Uses decode with the uart decoder and the right line
Passes the baud rate as an option
Reports the decoded text from the data row
Mentions framing/parity warnings when present

evals.prompt: Which protocols can this ATK-Logic installation decode, and can it do Modbus?
evals.expected_output: Runs decoders (optionally --search) and reports that the GUI ships the sigrok collection, lists relevant decoders such as ir_nec/uart/i2c/spi, and explains that modbus needs the uart decoder stacked upstream, which the skill does not host yet.
expectations: Runs decoders to list what is installed
Names concrete decoder ids
Explains the stacking limit for modbus instead of claiming it works

evals.prompt: The RS485 line on channel 0 carries Modbus RTU at 115200 8N1. Decode the register reads and tell me whether the CRCs are valid.
evals.expected_output: Runs decode with a stacked chain (--protocol uart+modbus, --ch rx=0, --option baudrate=115200, direction options if needed) and reports slave id, function, address/quantity and CRC status from the cs/sc rows; explains the chain syntax and the direction options if the first attempt lands in the wrong row.
expectations: Uses a decoder chain rather than claiming Modbus cannot be decoded
Passes the baud rate as an option
Reports slave id, function and CRC validity
Explains channel/direction mapping when the frame decodes into the wrong row

evals.prompt: I have no I2C signal generator. Can I still check that the I2C decoding works?
evals.expected_output: Explains the simulation route: run an HDL testbench (Icarus Verilog) to produce a VCD, convert it with `sim --vcd ... --scl scl --sda sda_line --rate 10m --out DIR`, then decode the resulting directory with `decode --protocol i2c --ch scl=0 --ch sda=1`. Notes that simulation validates decoder wiring but not real levels or glitches.
expectations: Mentions `sim --vcd` and that it writes capture.json plus channel_N.bin
Runs decode on the produced directory with --ch scl=... / --ch sda=...
States the boundary: simulation cannot validate levels, glitches or trigger behaviour

evals.prompt: I keep saving projects from the GUI into the same folder. Summarise new ones automatically.
evals.expected_output: Uses `watch --dir <folder> --once` (or without --once for a polling loop) and reports samples/channels/frequency for each new .atkdl file, mentioning --interval for the loop.
expectations: Calls watch with --dir
Explains --once versus the polling loop with --interval
Reports per-project samples, channels and frequency

evals.prompt: My captured waveform has 23 tiny glitches. I want statistics without them.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs the native capture with `usb capture ... --remove-glitches N` (or re-analyses with that flag) and shows that the glitch count drops to 0 while the frequency stays the same.
expectations: Uses usb capture with --remove-glitches
Explains that short pulses are absorbed, not dropped
Reports the glitch count before and after

evals.prompt: The analyzer only has a simple trigger. I need to catch an event that only matters after another edge happened first.
evals.expected_output: Runs `find SOURCE --stage CH:STATE --stage CH:STATE [--within ...]` on an existing capture: it locates stage 1, then looks ahead for stage 2 inside the window, and reports the matching sample indices/times. Explains that the hardware trigger is single-stage, so staged conditions are resolved after acquisition.
expectations: Uses the find command with at least two --stage arguments
Explains that staged conditions are resolved after acquisition, not by the hardware trigger
Reports hit start/end samples or times, and mentions --within for bounding the window

evals.prompt: The product blinks three times when I switch modes. Give me the timing and duty of each blink.
evals.expected_output: Captures the PWM pin (1 MHz x 5 s is enough) and runs `bursts SOURCE --ch N`, then reports each burst's start, duration, duty and frequency plus the gaps, instead of describing the waveform by eye.
expectations: Uses the bursts command on the capture
Reports per-burst duration, duty and frequency, and the gaps between bursts
Notes that frequency must come from the median edge interval, not edge counting
